findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses status: String and two independent bools (is_validated, is_sent), making every boolean combination representable including illegal ones (e.g. status="draft" with is_sent=true, or status="sent" with is_sent=false). The compiler cannot enforce valid state transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Any code path can place the ledger into an inconsistent state silently. Validation checks become runtime-only and easily skipped, leading to corrupted ledger records or incorrect downstream processing.
findings.fix: Replace status: String and is_validated: bool with a LedgerStatus enum (e.g. Draft, Validated, Sent) that encodes all lifecycle states. Remove is_sent entirely — it is redundant with the enum variant. The only reachable states are the enum variants.

findings.problem: status is a public String field. Any code can set it to any string value ("draft", "SENT", "sent", "", "deleted", "corrupted"), making the type system useless for enforcing domain invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream consumers cannot pattern-match on status safely. Typos or casing mismatches create silent bugs. No domain-level validation at the type boundary.
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with a private LedgerStatus enum and expose only domain-meaningful operations (e.g. as_str(), transitions). The enum should be non-exhaustive if future states may be added.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag. True/false provide no domain semantics and cannot prevent the invalid state of being both validated and unvalidated simultaneously (when combined with is_sent).
findings.failure_mode: The bool flag is independently mutable. Code can set is_validated without touching is_sent or status, creating incoherent state. No transition invariants are enforced.
findings.fix: Fold is_validated into the LedgerStatus enum. There should be no separate bool for lifecycle — the enum variant itself is the proof of state.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a redundant boolean lifecycle flag. It duplicates information already in status (if status contains "sent") but is independently mutable, creating contradiction potential.
findings.failure_mode: status could say "draft" while is_sent is true — a contradiction that breaks any consumer assuming sent implies the ledger has been transmitted.
findings.fix: Remove is_sent entirely. The LedgerStatus enum should have a Sent variant that implicitly proves sentness. Remove the separate boolean field.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes LedgerWorkflow by value and mutates it in place (mut item). The functional core should return a new immutable value rather than mutating. This violates the pure-deterministic-core principle.
findings.failure_mode: Mutation introduces hidden side-effect ordering dependencies. The function cannot be reasoned about compositionally and is harder to test deterministically.
findings.fix: Define mark_sent as a pure method on an immutable reference, returning Result<LedgerWorkflow, TransitionError> that constructs a new immutable ledger in the Sent state. The old value is dropped.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no precondition checks. It unconditionally sets status to "sent" and is_sent to true regardless of whether the ledger was previously validated or is in a legal transition state.
findings.failure_mode: A draft ledger can be marked sent without ever being validated. This bypasses the validation gate, potentially sending unreviewed/invalid ledger entries.
findings.fix: Use a typed transition method that validates preconditions: e.g. fn validate(self) -> Result<Self, Error> then fn send(self) -> Result<Self, Error>. Each transition checks its own preconditions and returns a typed error on failure.

findings.problem: All fields of LedgerWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate any field directly without going through domain methods. This defeats encapsulation and invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: External code can do item.is_sent = false to unsent a ledger, or item.status = "corrupted" to corrupt the state, bypassing all domain methods.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide constructor and transition methods only. The struct should be unrepresentable in an invalid state by construction.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> stores a timestamp but there is no domain value object for timestamps. Any u64 value is accepted, including zero, overflow, or nonsensical past/future values.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid timestamps could be stored (epoch 0 = 1970, or future-dated entries), breaking time-based queries and audit trails.
findings.fix: Introduce a SentTimestamp newtype with a fallible constructor that validates the value is within an acceptable epoch range. Store Option<SentTimestamp> instead of Option<u64>.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any throughput/latency claim
no profiler data for allocation profiles of LedgerWorkflow construction
no allocation analysis (try_reserve or Vec::with_capacity not applicable here, but no heap-allocation audit)
no second-ring evidence: no property tests, no fuzz harness, no state-machine transition tests
no command evidence: cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy not executed
no formal state-machine model for LedgerWorkflow transitions
residual_risk: High. The entire domain model is representable in illegal states via primitive String and bool fields with no transition guards. This is the canonical 'invalid state ledger typestate' anti-pattern the crate title warns against. Static review only; no commands executed. The struct must be re-modelled with a closed enum typestate, private fields, and validated transition methods before any production use.
